summary.brief: A mechanic replaces the crankshaft seal on a 1996 Nissan Altima.
summary.detailed: The technician lifts the car, removes the lower mudguard and the two drive belts, then breaks the tension‑adjusting nut on the crankshaft pulley. Using a puller and a light impact‑wrench tap, the large keyed pulley is removed, exposing a suspect old crank seal. The new seal is oriented with the stamped side facing outward, hand‑seated and checked for even seating, then tapped flush with a dead‑blow hammer. The pulley is reinstalled, the bolt is first hand‑tightened and finally torqued to the specified 101‑112 ft‑lb, after which the mudguard is re‑installed.

action.detailed: Remove the crankshaft pulley with a puller, extract the old seal, press the new seal into place with a dead‑blow hammer, reinstall the pulley and torque its bolt to specification.

summary.brief: A mechanic lifts the 1996 Nissan Altima, removes the front crankshaft pulley and installs a new crankshaft seal.
summary.detailed: The car is raised on a yellow lift and the front mud guard is removed to expose the crankshaft pulley. The drive belt is taken off and the tensioner nut is loosened. A puller is positioned on the pulley, the nut is backed off a little and the pulley is driven off the crankshaft, revealing the old seal that is keyed to the shaft. The old seal is taken out, its orientation noted, and a new seal is pressed onto the crankshaft with a seal‑puller and light taps from a dead‑blow hammer, taking care to avoid bending the metal and to seat it on the correct side.

summary_sent_to_llm.title: 1996 Nissan Altima Crank Seal Replacement
summary_sent_to_llm.description:
Crank shaft seal replacement on a 1996 Nissan Altima with a KA24DE engine.

This repair should apply to any 1993-2001 Altima with a KA24DE engine.
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The technician lifts the car, removes the lower mudguard and the two drive belts, then breaks the tension‑adjusting nut on the crankshaft pulley. Using a puller and a light impact‑wrench tap, the large keyed pulley is removed, exposing a suspect old crank seal. The new seal is oriented with the stamped side facing outward, hand‑seated and checked for even seating, then tapped flush with a dead‑blow hammer. The pulley is reinstalled, the bolt is first hand‑tightened and finally torqued to the specified 101‑112 ft‑lb, after which the mudguard is re‑installed.
action_list: Install crank seal and reinstall pulley
Install and secure the crankshaft seal and pulley
